title: How to Split Expenses With Roommates
excerpt: Agree on a fair split, record payments, and settle shared costs without confusion.
introduction: Shared living is easier when everyone understands what is shared and how it will be paid. The fictional example below uses an equal split in PKR; roommates can agree on another method.
author: Hisab Ki Kitab Editorial Team

blocks.text: One person pays the internet bill, another buys groceries, and nobody knows the final balance.

Agree on eligible expenses and the split before spending. Equal shares may fit common supplies, while room size or actual use may justify a different arrangement. Separate what someone owes from what they already paid.
Three roommates agree to share PKR 12,000 of common costs equally. Ali paid PKR 8,000, Sana paid PKR 4,000, and Omar paid nothing yet.
PKR 12,000 ? 3 = PKR 4,000 each. Omar pays Ali PKR 4,000; all three then carry the same net cost.

items: Agree which costs are shared and which are personal.
Choose equal shares or record agreed percentages that total 100%.
Save receipts and record the payer, date, amount, and participants.
Review the ledger together on a regular settlement date.
Mark transfers as settlements so they are not counted as a second expense.
Adding a personal purchase to a shared receipt.
Changing a split after others have already paid.
Counting a reimbursement as new household spending.

blocks.text: Make it easier to keep going
Write down how you will handle a move-out, guests, and partial months before those situations arise.
A clear agreement and a shared record matter more than a complicated formula. Confirm disputed costs before settling.

sources.title: CFPB: Spending and cash-flow tools (background; roommate example is original)

faqs.question: Should roommates always split expenses equally?
faqs.answer: Only if everyone agrees that an equal share is fair for that cost. Room size, use and agreements can support a different split.

faqs.question: How often should shared expenses be settled?
faqs.answer: Pick a predictable date and agree how receipts, reimbursements and move-out balances will be recorded.
